subject: Choosing cabinet finishes and handles
hook: Antique gold or matt black handles? One warms a kitchen, one sharpens it.
ig:
Antique gold or matt black handles? One warms a kitchen, one sharpens it.

Both are popular, both look good. They just do different jobs.

A: Antique gold
+ Adds warmth to charcoal, black woodgrain and oak-effect doors.
+ Catches light in the evening, which suits darker kitchens.
- Wants a soft cloth now and then to keep its sheen.

B: Matt black
+ Crisp, graphic contrast on matt white and pale finishes.
+ Ties in with black taps, lighting and window frames.
- Water marks can show on handles near the sink.

One useful test: hold both against your door sample and your tap. Whichever ties those two together usually wins.

Which would you pick, and what finish would it go on? Tell us in the comments. It helps us see what people are planning for next year.
fb:
Sunday handle debate: antique gold or matt black?

Gold warms up charcoal and wood-effect doors and glows a bit under evening lights. Black gives a sharp contrast on white and pale finishes and pairs neatly with black taps and light fittings.

Neither is wrong. The trick is to hold both against your door sample and your tap and see which pulls them together.
